experiment_2_simulation_hourly_cadence.description: Simulation test rows subsampled every 12th row to simulate hourly cadence. Feature vectors reconstructed from t5 columns of each subsampled row. Same domain as training; only cadence changes.

target_compatibility_audit.simulation_target: Binary label = HelioMesh safety rule applied to t+30min snapshot (6 independent horizon steps at 5-min intervals beyond the 30-min look-back window).
target_compatibility_audit.omni2_evaluation_target: Binary label = HelioMesh safety rule applied to the OMNI2 snapshot at position t+1 (1 hour after the last window step). This represents a 1-hour ahead prediction, not 30-min ahead.
target_compatibility_audit.classification: DOMAIN-SHIFT / TRANSFER TEST — the OMNI2 evaluation combines three mismatches: (1) cadence mismatch (hourly vs 5-min), (2) domain shift (real OMNI2-style distributions vs simulation distributions), (3) target mismatch (t+1h ahead vs t+30min ahead). It does NOT measure temporal spacecraft prediction accuracy.

scientific_conclusion: Simulation 5-min benchmark (frozen): macro_f1=0.9708. Simulation downsampled to hourly cadence (Exp-2): macro_f1=0.4329. OMNI2 hourly evaluation (Exp-3): macro_f1=0.4839. Total drop from Exp-1 to Exp-3: -0.4869. Cadence-only effect (Exp-1 to Exp-2): -0.5379 (110% of total drop). Residual domain/target effect (Exp-2 to Exp-3): --0.0510 (-10% of total drop). Primary cause diagnosis: A — cadence mismatch dominates. HONEST CONCLUSION: The OMNI2 evaluation is a DOMAIN-SHIFT / TRANSFER TEST, not a temporal prediction benchmark. Three simultaneous mismatches prevent drawing any conclusion about real spacecraft prediction accuracy from this result. The 0.4839 OMNI2 macro-F1 reflects these mismatches, not model quality on real data.
